$comment: SHARED CONTRACT -- the BLANK PREDICATE seam (virtual-column search/filter round, 2026-07-31).
THE QUESTION THIS SEAM ASKS: 'is this cell empty?' -- and it now has to be answered TWICE,
once in Python and once in SQL, about the same cell.
Python : `crud.is_blank_value(v)`      (== `crud.clean_str_value(v) == ""`)
SQL    : `crud.blank_sql_condition(c)` (== `c IS NULL OR c = ''`)
They do not agree by construction. `str.strip()` removes 29 codepoints; `=` removes none and
`btrim(c)` would remove exactly one (U+0020). A cell holding a bare TAB is empty to Python and
non-empty to SQL, so a row the grid PAINTS as the unresolved label would be MISSING from a
search for that label -- a silent under-report, which is the failure class this file exists to
make loud.
WHAT MAKES THE PAIR AGREE ANYWAY -- AND WHY THAT IS NOT ENOUGH
The 2026-07-31 user ruling was to block the divergent input at the write boundary rather than
teach SQL Python's whitespace table. `crud.normalize_stored_text` + `crud.cast_value_by_type`
do that, and AFTER them the two spellings are the same predicate BY CONSTRUCTION.
This contract deliberately does NOT assume that normalization ran. It scores three things:
(W) the write boundary really does remove every divergent input        -- INV-BP-W*
(E) the two spellings agree on every value that CAN be stored          -- INV-BP-E*
(X) on values that BYPASS the boundary the two spellings disagree,
exactly as recorded, so the exposure has a number instead of a hope -- INV-BP-X1
A vector that assumed normalization always ran would assert its own powerlessness: legacy
rows predate it, and any writer that does not funnel through `apply_batch_updates` reopens it.
HOW TO RUN
server (all axes except the Postgres dialect):
conda run -n assy_manager python -m pytest contracts/blank_predicate/ -q -rs
(reaches the default suite via server/tests/test_blank_predicate_contract.py)
server, Postgres dialect axis (opt-in, READ-ONLY, scalar SELECTs, no table touched):
ASSY_CONTRACT_PG_URL=postgresql://... conda run -n assy_manager python -m pytest contracts/blank_predicate/ -q -rs
client:
node contracts/blank_predicate/client_harness.mjs
THE DIALECT TRAP, AND WHY IT IS PINNED RATHER THAN IGNORED
`pytest server/tests/` runs on sqlite:///:memory:. Production is PostgreSQL 18.3. The two
dialects DO NOT RENDER NUMBERS THE SAME WAY: `cast(7.0 as varchar)` is '7.0' on SQLite and
'7' on Postgres. So a render axis scored only on the suite's dialect would bless a divergence
that does not exist in production and miss one that does. `dialect_facts` records both,
measured, and `test_the_suite_dialect_is_not_production` fails if anyone forgets.
Rule 1 of the contract-keeper charter: every expected answer says where it came from, and
NONE of them may be 'whatever the implementation returned'. Four sources are used here.
expectation_sources.spec: A stated rule of the system, quoted at the case. Chiefly `server/virtual_join_executor.py` module docstring: the empty test 'must mean the same thing as the rest of the system', and `_resolve_one`'s three-way rule (left value / joined value / unresolved label).
expectation_sources.declared_type: What the declared type of the column means. A `number` column holds a NUMBER, so 7.0 and 7 are the same value and must render alike; a `string` column holds TEXT, so '0.0' is three characters and is not a number at all.
expectation_sources.identity_rule: The system's own value-identity rule, which predates this round and is not part of the implementation under test: `crud.get_row_by_business_key` compares `str(key_value).strip()`, and composite business keys are joined from `clean_str_value` parts. Surrounding whitespace is therefore already NOT part of a value's identity anywhere in this system.
expectation_sources.measured: An observed answer, recorded with the date and the engine version. Used ONLY for dialect facts and for `known_defects` pins -- never as the contract value for an axis.

$comment: The 29 codepoints Python's `str.strip()` removes -- i.e. every `chr(cp).isspace()`.
DERIVED, NOT TRANSCRIBED: the scorer recomputes this set from the running interpreter and
fails if it differs. A hand-typed list would be a 30th thing to keep in sync, and it would
silently drift on a Python upgrade.
Four of them surprise people and are in the corpus for that reason: U+001C..U+001F are the
ASCII file/group/record/unit separators. They are NOT Unicode White_Space, but Python strips
them. Anyone writing a SQL character class 'covering Unicode whitespace' would omit all four.
whitespace_class.$why_that_gap_matters: btrim(c) covers 1 of 29. A SQL spelling built on it would be RIGHT for a leading space and WRONG for a tab, which is the worst shape a predicate can have: it looks tested.

$comment: role -> {file, fn, status}. The NAME is part of the contract. A rename must break the scorer
loudly rather than quietly stop covering an axis -- `client2/tests/split_registry_harness.mjs`
died in its extraction step for weeks because nothing asserted the symbols still existed.
status: `live` = must exist now. `pending` = authored ahead of the implementation, quiet, and
must carry $owner and $blocks.

invariants.name: the two spellings agree on every value the write boundary can leave in storage
invariants.why: This is the seam. If they disagree on a storable value, a row that displays the unresolved label is missing from a search for it.
invariants.kills: any SQL spelling that tests `c = ''` alone while Python strips -- and equally any Python spelling that stops stripping while SQL does not.

invariants.name: NULL is blank in BOTH spellings, and the SQL one answers TRUE, never UNKNOWN
invariants.why: `_resolve_one` case (1) -- no right row -- arrives as NULL and must fold into the unresolved label. In SQL three-valued logic `btrim(c) = ''` on a NULL column evaluates to UNKNOWN, which a WHERE clause treats as NOT MATCHED. That single omission makes a blank filter miss EVERY unmatched row, which is the largest possible under-report on this seam.
invariants.kills: `btrim(c) = ''`, `c = ''`, `length(trim(c)) = 0` -- every spelling that forgets the NULL arm. All three look correct in a unit test seeded with non-NULL rows.

invariants.name: 0 and '0' and '0.0' and ' 0 ' are NOT blank in either spelling
invariants.why: A declared zero is a value. `v || dflt` and `if not v` are the standing trap in this codebase (map_seam known_defect D1 destroys a declared `phys_edge_margin: 0`), and an emptiness predicate is exactly where it comes back.
invariants.kills: `not v`, `if not str(v).strip()` used as a truthiness test on a numeric zero; `coalesce(nullif(c,''),'0') = '0'`-style folding.

invariants.name: blank(v) is TRUE if and only if render(v) is the empty string, in each spelling separately
invariants.why: This is the coupling the seam actually needs and it is checkable without deciding whose trailing-whitespace answer is right. A spelling where `blank('\t')` is true but `render('\t')` is '\t' contradicts itself: the row is counted as unresolved by the filter and painted as non-empty by the grid.
invariants.kills: the natural half-fix -- adding a trim to the emptiness test and leaving the value/render path untrimmed.

invariants.name: the two spellings render the same text for every storable value
invariants.why: A search compares TEXT. If Python compares 'A' and SQL compares 'A\t', a filter written from what the operator sees returns nothing.
invariants.kills: `cast(col as String)` paired with a Python side that strips -- the exact pair in `main.get_column_filter_condition` today.

invariants.name: no divergent value survives the write boundary
invariants.why: The 2026-07-31 user ruling: block the input rather than teach SQL Python's whitespace table. Stated as a POST-CONDITION, not a mechanism -- refusing the write and normalizing the value both satisfy it, and the contract has no business picking.
invariants.kills: a normalizer that handles `''` and `' '` (the two everyone thinks of) and lets `'\t'` through.

invariants.name: after a write through the funnel, the two spellings agree about that stored row
invariants.why: The round trip, end to end, through the real `apply_batch_updates`. It is the one assertion here that cannot be satisfied by a coincidence in either half.
invariants.kills: any future writer added to `apply_row_update_internal` that sets a column without going through `cast_value_by_type`.

invariants.name: on a value that BYPASSED the boundary, the two spellings disagree exactly as recorded
invariants.why: The safety of the short SQL spelling rests entirely on the storage invariant. This pins the size of what that invariant is holding back, so the day someone proposes a bulk loader or a snapshot restore the cost is written down instead of rediscovered. It is red in the OTHER direction if the disagreement ever narrows -- e.g. if a trim is quietly added to the SQL side, which would mean the two halves are no longer the pair this file describes.
invariants.kills: a silent unilateral change to either spelling.

invariants.name: exactly ONE SQL spelling of blank exists in server/
invariants.why: Duplication guard, counted by AST. `crud.blank_sql_condition` was extracted precisely so the rule has one home; a second copy re-creates the state it was extracted from, and the copy is what goes stale. The third copy always arrives during review, not before it.
invariants.kills: a second `or_(c.is_(None), c == '')` written inline at a new filter site.

invariants.name: the client does not carry its own unresolved-label literal
invariants.why: The label is a per-declaration server value (`unresolved_label`). A client that writes it down can disagree with the server about what text a row even displays -- and then 'search for what you see' has two answers.
invariants.kills: `const UNRESOLVED = '...'` appearing in the grid path.

$comment: NAMED, ATTRIBUTED, SELF-CANCELLING pins -- same semantics as contracts/map_seam/vectors.json.
PINNED (recorded value observed)  -> reported under its id, green.
STALE  (contract value observed)  -> RED IN THE OTHER DIRECTION; the defect was fixed and the
pin has silently stopped asserting anything.
CHANGED SHAPE (neither)           -> red, louder.
A pin may never agree with the contract value it stands in for.
EMPTY as of 2026-07-31: DUP1 and NUM1 were both CLEARED in the CSV-export round,
each per its own `clears_when`.
DUP1 - main.get_column_filter_condition (blank AND notBlank) and
enrichment_analysis._human_resolved_cells (notBlank) now delegate to
crud.blank_sql_condition / crud.not_blank_sql_condition. Counts went 2->1
and 3->1. Verified by re-running the contract's own fault injection:
patching crud.blank_sql_condition NOW turns the AG-Grid blank-filter tests
red, which is exactly what it failed to do when DUP1 was written.
NUM1 - cast_value_by_type falls back to float() when the int() branch rejects a
repr with no '.', so 1e+16 and 1e-05 store instead of being refused.
nan/inf stay refused on purpose. `float_1e16.stored_as` now stands.
FLOAT_EXPONENT was deliberately NOT chased (Lead PM ruling 2026-07-31) and stays
in declared_divergences below, where it keeps asserting that both sides still give
the recorded answers - so it cannot rot into a green that means nothing.
NOT agreement. Each side keeps its own recorded answer ON PURPOSE or PENDING A RULING, and
the contract asserts each side still gives the answer recorded here. Neither is called wrong.

FLOAT_EXPONENT.title: a float large enough to reach exponent notation renders differently on the two sides
FLOAT_EXPONENT.why: `clean_str_value` folds any integral float through `str(int(v))`, which never uses exponent notation. Postgres float8 output uses shortest-round-trip, which does. Both are lossless; they are simply different spellings of one number, and a text comparison sees two different strings.
FLOAT_EXPONENT.reach: only a `number` column whose magnitude reaches 1e16. No production column measured on 2026-07-31 holds one. Recorded so the seam is not later assumed total.
FLOAT_EXPONENT.decision: Lead PM. Not resolved by this contract.

$comment: MEASURED, with provenance. These are not contract values -- they are the reason the render
axis cannot be scored on the suite's dialect alone.
dialect_facts.$production: PostgreSQL 18.3 on x86_64-windows, server_encoding UTF8, extra_float_digits=1
dialect_facts.$why_it_is_pinned: The dispatch that opened this round expected `col::text` to render 7.0 as '7.0'. That is TRUE on SQLite and FALSE on Postgres, because a `number` column materializes as `double precision` (models.init_dynamic_models maps 'number' -> Float). Scoring the render axis on the suite's dialect would therefore have reported a divergence production does not have.

$comment: READ-ONLY, statement-timeout-bounded scan of the live database, 2026-07-31. Recorded because
INV-BP-X1 is about EXPOSURE and exposure without a number is a feeling. Not a contract value.
Re-measure rather than quote: this block goes stale by the day.
production_scan.where: all 13 are in `file_ingestion_logs` (an operations log, not a grid-backed data table)
production_scan.reading: The emptiness half of the divergence is LATENT in stored data, not active. That is a reason the seam is safe today, and NOT a reason the pair may stay unequal: nothing in the schema prevents the next bulk path from putting one there.

$comment: One expected verdict per input per axis, each with its source. Inputs are given as CODEPOINT
ARRAYS, never as literal characters: U+00A0 and U+3000 are invisible in an editor and a
well-meaning save can turn either into U+0020 without a visible diff.
blank      -- expected answer of BOTH spellings to 'is this empty?'
render     -- expected canonical comparison text, the thing a search matches against
stored_as  -- what the write boundary must leave in the column, as a codepoint array,
or null for SQL NULL. INV-BP-W1 is scored against this.
`stored_as: null` does NOT mean 'refused'. The ruling was that the divergent value must not be
STORABLE; mapping it to NULL satisfies that, and so would a 400. The contract scores the
post-condition.

cases.$why: `_resolve_one` case (1): the LEFT OUTER JOIN found no right row, so every exposed column arrives NULL and must fold into the unresolved label. If SQL answers UNKNOWN here instead of TRUE, a blank filter loses every unmatched row.

`_resolve_one` case (2): the right row exists and its value is empty. The virtual_join_executor docstring measures this at 26.27% of bonding_log -> core_wafer_map. Dropping it reads a quarter of the table as 'has a value'.
단일 스페이스 -- 두 철자가 우연히 일치하는 유일한 공백. btrim의 기본 문자집합이 딱 이 한 글자라서, 이 케이스만 보고 SQL이 맞다고 결론내면 나머지 28개를 놓친다.
이 라운드를 연 바로 그 입력. Python은 비었다고, 순진한 SQL은 안 비었다고 답한다. 사용자 판정(2026-07-31) 「그냥 \t 같은데 안들어가게 막아」의 대상이기도 하다.
엑셀 붙여넣기의 실제 산물. 셀 안의 줄바꿈이 단독으로 남으면 이 값이 된다.
Windows 클립보드 경로. 두 글자라서 '길이가 0인가'로 판정하는 구현을 잡는다.
U+00A0. 웹에서 복사한 값에 흔하고 화면에서는 스페이스와 구별되지 않는다. Postgres의 `[[:space:]]` 클래스에도 들어가지 않아 정규식으로 고치려는 시도까지 같이 잡는다.
U+3000. 한글 IME에서 한자 모드일 때 스페이스가 이 글자로 들어간다 -- 이 시스템의 운영 환경에서 가장 현실적인 비-U+0020 공백이다.
U+001F. Python이 strip하지만 Unicode White_Space가 아니다. 「유니코드 공백을 다 덮었다」고 쓴 SQL 문자 클래스는 U+001C..U+001F 네 개를 반드시 빠뜨린다 -- 그 구현을 떨어뜨리려고 코퍼스에 있다.
섞인 공백. 바깥쪽이 U+0020이라 btrim이 양끝을 벗겨내고도 가운데가 남는다 -- 「btrim 붙였으니 됐다」를 정확히 이 케이스가 반증한다.
선언된 0. `v || dflt` 계열이 값을 기본값으로 바꾸는 함정(map_seam D1)이 공백 판정에서 되돌아오는 자리다.
string 컬럼의 '0.0'은 숫자가 아니라 세 글자다. float 접기(7.0 -> '7')를 문자열에까지 적용하는 구현이면 여기서 '0'이 되어 떨어진다.
0과 공백을 한 케이스에 넣는다. 「전부 공백이면 빈 값」과 「공백은 값의 일부가 아니다」가 서로 다른 규칙임을 강제한다.
평범한 비어있지 않은 값. 이게 통과하지 않으면 나머지 채점은 의미가 없다.
공백 판정은 두 철자가 일치한다(둘 다 비어있지 않다). 갈라지는 것은 RENDER다 -- Python은 'A', 순진한 SQL은 'A\t'. 검색이 실제로 비교하는 것이 render이므로, 공백 축만 본 계약은 이 결함을 통째로 놓친다.
위와 같은 축이되 U+0020이라 btrim 한 줄로 고쳐진다. 둘을 같이 두면 '고쳤다'가 어느 범위까지인지가 드러난다.
앞쪽 공백. ltrim만 있는/rtrim만 있는 구현을 가른다.
number 컬럼의 7.0과 7은 같은 수다. 두 철자가 같은 텍스트를 내야 한다는 요구는 구현이 아니라 선언 타입에서 나온다. (실측: Postgres float8은 '7', SQLite는 '7.0' -- dialect_facts 참조.)
정수가 아닌 float. 7.0 접기를 모든 float에 적용하는 구현이면 7이 되어 떨어진다.
선언된 숫자 0. `if not value` 한 줄이면 여기서 빈 값이 된다 -- 헌장이 코퍼스에 0을 반드시 넣으라고 하는 이유가 이 케이스다.
선언된 발산 케이스. render는 계약이 정하지 않는다 -- `declared_divergences.FLOAT_EXPONENT`가 양쪽 답을 기록하고, 각 철자가 기록된 답을 계속 내는지만 채점한다. 총괄 판정 대상이다.

$comment: The client half of THIS seam is small and it is not the emptiness rule -- that rule lives
entirely on the server. What the client owns is (a) keying its FILTER behaviour off the
server's announcement rather than off its own guess, and (b) not writing down the label the
server sends.
RE-POINTED 2026-07-31 (second time today). The user ordered virtual-join columns to become
searchable, so `filter: false` is no longer the right answer and `virtual_columns` is no
longer where the label comes from. TWO PINS MOVED, NEITHER WAS DROPPED -- what they assert
is now the DISTINCTION rather than the old value:
was: 'the virtual columnDef declares filter: false'
now: 'the filter def is chosen by the ANNOUNCEMENT (`join_resolved_columns`), with
`filter: false` kept as the absent-announcement fallback'
was: 'the columnDef reads vc.unresolved_label' (positional -- literal within 4000 chars
of the first `unresolved_label`)
now: 'the label reaching the filter def is read off the SERVER ENTRY'
THE POSITIONAL ANCHOR WAS THE WEAK PART AND IT IS GONE. Proximity is not a property of the
code, it is a property of the file layout, and it broke the moment the label moved. Every
check below now anchors on a NAMED symbol extracted by name, so a rename is exit 2 (could
not score) rather than a false verdict in either direction.
WHY `join_resolved_columns` AND NOT `isVirtualColumn`: `virtual_columns` answers 'which
columns must the grid ADD', which OMITS `collide` -- a column stored on the left that the
server still resolves through the join. Keying filter behaviour off `isVirtualColumn` misses
every collide column silently. That is the whole reason the new key exists.
🔴 `collide` IS NOT LIVE ANYWHERE right now (`bonding_log.wafer_id` became `virtual_only`
when the user edited table_config), so it exists only in fixtures and in these assertions.
The fixture IS the only thing protecting it.

client_symbols.$comment: role -> {file, fn}. Extracted BY NAME. Missing symbol = EXIT 2 (could not score), never exit 0 and never a false pass -- the positional anchor this replaced produced exactly that.

virtual_column_filter.$why: the label is per-declaration server data; the client must READ it, and a filter on a virtual column must not be declared until the server can answer one

forbidden_client_literals.$note: the default `unresolved_label`. STILL GREEN and must stay green -- nothing hardcodes it.
forbidden_client_literals.$why_scoped: `doe_bands.js` legitimately owns its OWN rollup word for a different domain (ROLLUP_UNKNOWN) and `map_editor.js` uses it in prose comments. Scoping to the grid/read path is what keeps this check about THIS seam instead of about the character.

$comment: What the client must key its filter off, and what it must fall back to. Scored against
`buildColumnDefs`, extracted by name -- BOTH arms of the choice, in both column paths.
filter_behaviour.$why_forbidden: `isVirtualColumn` answers 'did /schema ADD this column', which omits every `collide` column. Keying the filter off it misses them silently -- the exact mistake this key exists to prevent.
filter_behaviour.$why_fallback: A server that announces `virtual_columns` but NOT `join_resolved_columns` is a PRE-CHANGE server: it contributes no condition for that name and returns the page UNFILTERED, while the client-side row model trims what is on screen. The rows then look filtered while `Matches:` stays at the unfiltered total. `filter: false` is the honest-degradation arm and must survive.

paths_that_must_consult_the_announcement.$why: the column exists only in the read payload
a STORED column whose filter the server evaluates against the joined value. It is NOT in `virtual_columns`, so only the announcement can find it.

$comment: Blank/NotBlank must be ABSENT on a join-resolved column and PRESENT on an ordinary stored
one. Scored in BOTH directions -- removing them from the wrong set is a real failure that
already happened once on 2026-07-31.
filter_options.$why_absent: The resolved value is a COALESCE whose last arm is `unresolved_label`, which `virtual_join_config` guarantees is a non-empty string. No row in such a column is EVER blank: `blank` matches nothing and `notBlank` matches everything, on every row, forever. Offering them is the UI making a claim it cannot keep. Measured before removal: blank -> 0 of 15,489, notBlank -> 15,489 of 15,489, while `equals <label>` returned 4,052.
filter_options.$why_present_on_stored: An ordinary stored column really can be NULL or empty, and its blank filter is answered by `crud.blank_sql_condition` -- the very predicate the SERVER half of this contract scores. Restricting the stored list too would delete a working control and silently narrow the seam this contract exists to pin.

editability.$comment: The announcement must NOT decide editability -- the same line the server half holds at `refuse_virtual_join_columns`, held independently here so neither side can move alone.
editability.$why: A collide column is a real stored column; writing it is how an operator overrides the joined value (the absent-only rule's 'left has a value' arm). Only its FILTER changes. And `editable` is not enforcement in either direction -- the server refuses the write; this flag only stops the grid offering an edit that would come back 400.

label_source.$comment: Re-pointed away from a positional anchor. The question is not 'are these two strings near each other' but 'where does the label reaching the filter def come from'.
label_source.$why: The label rides per declaration in `virtual_join_rules.json`. A site that renames it must see the new name on the next /schema. A constant, or a read from the wrong object, makes that declaration dead config.
